page_data.en:
Assault Case in Police Court
Dismissed by H.M. Registrar

THE case against Mr. D. G. J. Keet, who was charged by Mrs.
E. C. Palmer-Baker with having struck her on the face with
his closed fist on the evening on June 19, was dismissed in H M.
Police Court yesterday when Mr. C. H. Haines, Registrar, found the
defendant not guilty of the charge. Thus, the case of a couple of
unneighbourly "neighbours" in Passage 316, Route Paul Legendre,
was brought to a close.
Unlike the first session, in which Mrs. Palmer-Baker attempted
to conduct her own case, the complainant was represented by Mr.
Rapald McDonald yesterday. Mr. E. L. Hartopp appeared for
defendant.
In his summing-up' Mr. Haine said that he was struck by the fact
that complainant was an excitable
person and that it was possible that
she had thought that she had been
struck while she was struggling to
close her garden gate on the de-
fendant. The injury was of such
nature that it was quite possible that
she could have been struck by the
gate on its rebound: Mr. Haines re-
ferred to the evidence of complai-
nant's amah in which witness had
said that the mark was pink on the
next morning.
Mr. Hartopp's request for costs in
favour of the defendant, who he said
"was not very blessed in the world,"
was not granted by the Registrar.
Mrs. M. Cock was the first witness
called yesterday and she testified
that she was at Mrs. Palmer-Baker's
home, together with Mrs. M. E. Paus,
on June 19, leaving the house soon
after the evening news broadcast at
8 p.m. Mrs. Palmer-Baker was per-
fectly well and happy when they left
her.

Telephone Call Received
As soon as she got home, however,
Mrs. Cock received a telephone call
from Mrs. Palmer-Baker, asking her
to come back. The witness im-
mediately telephoned Mrs. Paus and
they returned. The plaintiff, accord-
ing to witness, had her right cheek
red and swollen.
Mrs. Paus testified that she and
Mrs. Cock had tea with plaintiff and
that they stayed there till a little
after 8.15 p.m. There was nothing
wrong with Mrs. Palmer-Paker's face
when they left her. Mrs. Paus then
took Mrs. Cock home.
A few minutes after her arrival at
home, Mrs. Paus answered a tele-
phone call from Mrs. Cock. She took
out her car and fetched Mrs. Cock.
Together they went to Mrs. Palmer-
Baker's home and witness noticed
that the plaintiff's right cheek had
blue marks and that she appeared
pale and excited.
She then took plaintiff and Mrs.
Cock to a police station and left her
there.
Cross-examined by Mr. Hartopp
with regard to the marks, Mrs. Paus
said she could not be sure whe-
ther they were red or blue since it
was dark. She stated that the
marks were definitely there.

Defendant Gives Evidence
Defendant was next called to give
evidence. Questioned by Mr. Hartopp,
Mr. Keet stated that, he was standing
outside, reading at about 8.30 p.m.
on June 19, when Mrs. Palmer-Baker
came out of her house and started
shouting at him. He tried to reason
with her but she continued shouting.
He then went into his house and
closed the door. A few minutes later
he heard Mrs. Palmer-Baker shouting
again. He opened the door and saw
her pointing to her right cheek. He
told her that he did not hit her and
turned away. A minute or so later,
as he was proceeding to the tram stop
near the I.S.S. Apartments in Avenue
Joffre, he saw her running toward
Route Loriox, shouting in Chinese,
"A foreigner hit me."

Wanted to Settle Affair
Cross-examined by plaintiff's
lawyer, Mr. Keet stated that he knew
that she did not want to see him or
talk with him, having on previous
occasions thrown his letters over the
fence, but added that he had to settle
the affair and that this was a good
opportunity to do so. The trouble,
it appeared, started over some al-
terations made to her house by Mrs.
Palmer-Baker, which resulted in the
back gate being continually open,
leaving Mr. Keet's yard open to petty
thieves.
Giving evidence in the afternoon,
Mrs. Mary M. Keet corroborated
much of what her husband had said.
She had seen her husband trying to
get a word with Mrs. Palmer-Baker;
she had witnessed the episode at the
gate; and later, after complainant
had received her alleged assault, she
had seen Mrs. Palmer-Baker swing
open the gate and "spring out like a
cat, livid in the face and malice in
her eyes."
At this point, Mr. Haines inter-
rupted, "I can't quite understand
what you mean by 'malice' in her
eyes."
Mrs. Keet explained: "She looked
very, very wicked."

Garden Gate Never Was Closed
During his cross-examination, Mr.
Keet stated that the garden gate was
never more than a foot from the
fence, and under such circumstances
it was practically impossible for any-
one to have struck Mrs. Palmer-
Baker with a closed fist. He also
stated that he had never raised his
hand to her.
face. Defendant then caught the
door and made an attempt to reason
with her, adding that Mrs. Palmer-
Baker started shouting at him, tell-
ing him that she did not wish to
speak with him and calling him a
"big bully."
Seeing it was hopeless to continue,
defendant released the door (perhaps
a little too suddenly) and walk-
ed away. He then heard Mrs.
Palmer-Baker come out, shouting
"Now you've hit me, eh?" and "I'll
call the police. I'll send you to
prison."
Defendant saw her pointing to her
right cheek and saw that it was
smudged. After telling her that he
did not hit her, the defendant turned
away. A minute or so later, as he
was proceeding to the tram stop
near the I.S.S. Apartments in Avenue
Joffre, he saw her running toward
Route Loriox, shouting in Chinese,
"A foreigner hit me."

巡捕房法庭殴打案
由英王陛下法院书记官驳回

E. C. 帕尔默-贝克夫人（Mrs. E. C. Palmer-Baker）指控 D. G. J. 基特先生（Mr. D. G. J. Keet）于6月19日晚用紧握的拳头击打其面部，针对基特先生的此案昨日在英王陛下警察法庭被驳回，当时书记官 C. H. 海恩斯先生（Mr. C. H. Haines）裁定被告对该项指控无罪。至此，发生在保罗·兰登路（Route Paul Legendre）316弄的一对不和睦“邻居”之间的案件画上了句号。

与帕尔默-贝克夫人试图自行辩护的首次庭审不同，昨日原告由拉帕尔德·麦克唐纳先生（Mr. Rapald McDonald）代理出庭。E. L. 哈托普先生（Mr. E. L. Hartopp）代表被告出庭。

海恩斯先生在总结陈词中表示，令他印象深刻的是，原告是一个易激动的人，很可能她在努力关上花园门以挡住被告时，以为自己遭到了击打。伤势的性质表明，她完全有可能是被反弹回来的门撞伤的。海恩斯先生提到了原告阿妈的证词，证人称第二天早上伤痕呈粉红色。

哈托普先生请求判给被告诉讼费，并称被告“在世上的福气不多”，但书记官未予批准。

M. 科克夫人（Mrs. M. Cock）是昨日第一位被传唤的证人，她作证说，6月19日她和 M. E. 保斯夫人（Mrs. M. E. Paus）一起在帕尔默-贝克夫人家中，晚上8点晚间新闻广播后不久便离开了。她们离开时，帕尔默-贝克夫人身体状况良好，心情愉快。

接到电话

然而，科克夫人一回到家，就接到了帕尔默-贝克夫人的电话，请她回去。证人立即打电话给保斯夫人，随后两人一同返回。据证人称，原告的右脸颊红肿。

保斯夫人作证说，她和科克夫人与原告一起喝茶，一直待到晚上8点15分过后。她们离开时，帕尔默-贝克夫人的脸上没有任何异样。随后，保斯夫人送科克夫人回家。

到家几分钟后，保斯夫人接听了科克夫人打来的电话。她开出汽车去接科克夫人。两人一同前往帕尔默-贝克夫人家，证人注意到原告右脸颊有青紫痕迹，且面色苍白，神情激动。

随后，她将原告和科克夫人送到巡捕房，并将原告留在那里。

在哈托普先生就伤痕进行盘问时，保斯夫人表示，由于天色已黑，她无法确定伤痕是红色还是青色。但她声明，伤痕确实存在。

被告提供证词

接下来传唤被告作证。在哈托普先生的询问下，基特先生陈述道，6月19日晚上8点30分左右，他正站在外面看书，这时帕尔默-贝克夫人从家里出来，开始对他大喊大叫。他试图与她讲理，但她继续叫喊。于是他走进屋内并关上了门。几分钟后，他听到帕尔默-贝克夫人再次叫喊。他打开门，看见她指着自己的右脸颊。他告诉她自己没有打她，然后转身离开。大约一分钟后，当他正前往霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）国际礼拜堂公寓（I.S.S. Apartments）附近的电车站时，看见她朝罗利奥路（Route Loriox）跑去，并用中文高喊：“外国人打我。”

希望解决此事

在原告律师的盘问下，基特先生表示，他知道她不想见他或与他交谈，因为她以前曾将他的信件扔过围墙，但他补充说，他必须解决这件事，而这是一个好机会。麻烦似乎起因于帕尔默-贝克夫人对其房屋进行的一些改建，导致后门一直敞开，使基特先生的院子容易遭受小偷小摸。

下午作证时，玛丽·M. 基特夫人（Mrs. Mary M. Keet） corroborated 了她丈夫所说的大部分内容。她看见丈夫试图与帕尔默-贝克夫人说句话；她目睹了门口发生的那一幕；后来，在原告声称遭到殴打后，她看见帕尔默-贝克夫人猛地推开大门，“像猫一样跳出来，脸色铁青，眼中带着恶意。”

此时，海恩斯先生打断道：“我不太明白你所说的她眼中的‘恶意’是什么意思。”

基特夫人解释道：“她看起来非常、非常邪恶。”

花园门从未关闭

在受盘问期间，基特先生表示，花园门离围栏从未超过一英尺，在这种情况下，任何人实际上都不可能用紧握的拳头击中帕尔默-贝克夫人。他还表示，他从未对她举起过手。
脸。被告随即抓住门，试图与她讲理，并补充说，帕尔默-贝克夫人开始对他大喊大叫，告诉他她不想和他说话，并称他为“大恶霸”。
见继续下去已无希望，被告松开了门（也许有点太突然），然后走开了。随后他听到帕尔默-贝克夫人出来说：“现在你打我了，嗯？”以及“我要叫警察。我要把你送进监狱。”
被告看见她指着自己的右脸颊，并看到上面有污迹。在告诉她自己没有打她之后，被告转身离开。大约一分钟后，当他正前往霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）国际礼拜堂公寓（I.S.S. Apartments）附近的电车站时，看见她朝罗利奥路（Route Loriox）跑去，并用中文高喊：“外国人打我。”

“He Bit My Dog’s Eye,” Witness Sobs
Briton Faces Court For
Assaulting Elderly Lady

Mr. D. O. J. Keet, Briton, was charged with assaulting and hitting Mrs. Evelyn Catherine Palmer-Baker with a clenched fist by Registrar C. H. Haines in the British Police Court yesterday. Mr. Keet pleaded not guilty to the charge and the case was adjourned to Monday 10 a.m. pending medical evidence in connection with the alleged assault.

Mr. Palmer-Baker, an elderly woman, claimed that Mr. Keet hit her with a clenched fist at 8:30 p.m. June 19, when, after escorting her friends out of her house 316 Route Paul Legendre, House 3, she met Mr. Keet, who blamed her for not closing the gate of the lane and hit her on the right cheek with a clenched fist.

She further claimed that she rushed out to call a policeman, but as she could not find one, she went to the Avenue Petain Police Station, and then went to the Country Hospital where she obtained a medical certificate from Dr. Bowan.

Cross-examined by Mr. E. L. Hartopp, defense attorney, Mrs. Palmer-Baker admitted that in that lane there were three houses, owned by the occupants, and that the path in front of the houses was enclosed by a gate which was closed because of the numerous thefts in that district.

On the night of the alleged assault, Mr. Hartopp suggested, Mr. Keet met Mrs. Palmer-Baker and wanted to speak with her. Instead of answering, she walked past him and slammed her garden gate at him, and that it was not a punch from Mr. Keet that bruised her face,

but that it was the gate when it bounced back on her. Mrs. Palmer-Baker, nearly in tears maintained that she was hit by the defendant. Mr. Hartopp hinted that relations between the two neighbors were strained, and told the complainant that in view of her state of nervousness she imagined that Mr. Keet had hit her, and asked her to reconsider her statements. Mrs. Palmer-Baker at this point openly cried, and in a choking voice said, “I have been ill since Mr. Keet moved into the house next to mine.”

Registrar Haines told Mrs. Palmer-Baker to rest, and five minutes later Mr. Hartopp resumed his cross-examination. At this point the complainant was beginning to get confused, and said that Mr. Keet kept bees, and that “he bit my dog in the eye”. People in the courtroom chuckled.

“I understand that you keep a savage dog,” Mr. Hartopp stated.
“He is my Scotty, and I love him,” Mrs. Palmer-Baker replied. Continuing Mrs. Palmer-Baker said, “Mr. Keet told the police on me, when I started building a new window.”

Mrs. Palmer-Baker’s amah testified that she saw a bruise of her employer’s cheek, but stated that she did not see Mr. Keet hit her mistress. Before concluding, Registrar Haines told Mrs. Palmer-Baker that she could ask Dr. Bowan to testify for her, and adjourned the case to 10 a.m. Monday pending Dr. Bowan’s testimony.

“他咬了我狗的眼睛，”证人抽泣
英国人因袭击老妇人面临法庭审判

英国人 D. O. J. 基特先生（Mr. D. O. J. Keet）昨日在英王陛下警察法庭被书记官 C. H. 海恩斯指控袭击并用紧握的拳头殴打伊夫林·凯瑟琳·帕尔默-贝克夫人（Mrs. Evelyn Catherine Palmer-Baker）。基特先生对指控表示不认罪，案件延期至周一上午10点审理，以待与所谓袭击有关的医疗证据。

帕尔默-贝克夫人是一位老妇人，她声称基特先生于6月19日晚上8点30分用紧握的拳头打了她。当时，她在保罗·兰登路（Route Paul Legendre）3号316弄的家中送朋友出门后，遇到了基特先生，后者指责她没有关上弄堂的门，并用紧握的拳头击打了她的右脸颊。

她还声称，她冲出去叫警察，但因找不到警察，便去了贝当路（Avenue Petain）巡捕房，随后去了宏恩医院（Country Hospital），从鲍恩医生（Dr. Bowan）那里获得了一份医疗证明。

在辩护律师 E. L. 哈托普先生的盘问下，帕尔默-贝克夫人承认，该弄堂内有三栋房屋，归住户所有，房屋前的通道由一道门围住，由于该地区盗窃案频发，这道门通常是关闭的。

哈托普先生指出，在所谓袭击发生的当晚，基特先生遇见了帕尔默-贝克夫人并想与她交谈。她没有回答，而是从他身边走过，并当着他的面摔上了花园门，使她脸部淤青的并非基特先生的拳头，

而是门反弹回来时撞到了她。帕尔默-贝克夫人几乎落泪，坚持称是被告打了她。哈托普先生暗示两位邻居关系紧张，并告诉原告，鉴于她的神经紧张状态，她想象是基特先生打了她，并请她重新考虑自己的陈述。此时，帕尔默-贝克夫人公开哭了起来，哽咽着说：“自从基特先生搬到我隔壁的房子后，我就病了。”

海恩斯书记官让帕尔默-贝克夫人休息一下，五分钟后，哈托普先生恢复盘问。此时，原告开始变得语无伦次，她说基特先生养蜜蜂，而且“他咬了我狗的眼睛”。法庭里的人发出窃笑声。

“我了解到你养了一只凶猛的狗，”哈托普先生说。
“那是我的苏格兰梗犬，我爱它，”帕尔默-贝克夫人回答道。帕尔默-贝克夫人接着说：“当我开始建造新窗户时，基特先生向警察告发了我。”

帕尔默-贝克夫人的阿妈作证说，她看到了雇主脸颊上的淤青，但表示她没有看到基特先生殴打女主人。结束前，海恩斯书记官告诉帕尔默-贝克夫人，她可以请鲍恩医生为她作证，并将案件延期至周一上午10点，以待鲍恩医生的证词。

page_data.en:
Briton Faces
Assault Charge

A story of continual animosity between two next-door neighbours that finally led to an alleged assault was unfolded in H. M. Police Court yesterday before Registrar C. H. Haines when Mrs. E. C. Palmer-Baker filed a charge of assault against Mr. D. G. J. Keet, accusing the latter of having struck her on the face with his closed fist. The assault was said to have taken place on the evening of June 19 at the entrance of the complainant's home in Passage 316, 3 Route Paul Legendre.

Mr Haines adjourned the hearing to next Monday in order that the complainant may call in witnesses to provide medical evidence.

Throughout yesterday's session, the complainant, an elderly woman, showed signs of evident distress and, at one stage of the cross-examination by the defendant's counsel, she broke down into tears. Mrs. Palmer-Baker was not represented in court: she was unfamiliar with the routine of the court and on numerous occasions she had to be enlightened on matters of legal procedure by the Registrar. Defendant was represented by Mr. E. L. Hartopp and pleaded not guilty.

Long-Standing Friction

The two principals in yesterday's case were next-door neighbours in Passage 316 of 3 Route Paul Legendre and it was revealed in court that friction between the two parties had been of long standing. It was brought out that Mrs. Palmer-Baker and Mr. Keet had been at logger-heads on various matters: they had disagreed on the right of way to the passage; complainant had objected to the flowers of the defendant growing into her garden; she had also objected to Mr. Keet's placing several boxes of bees on their common fence; on the other hand, defendant had disapproved of the gate to the passage being left opened; it was also the contention of the complainant that Mr. Keet had "told on her" when he informed the French police of her building operations which she had begun without obtaining permission.

It was this series of grievances which was said to have led to the assault that took place at about 8.30 on the evening of June 19. According to Mrs. Palmer-Baker's evidence, she had seen a couple of lady friends to the main gate of the passage. On the way back to her own house, Mr. Keet ran out of his house and shouted, "Why did you leave the gate open?" Complainant said she paid no notice to him as the gate was already closed.

Police Informed

Thereupon, as she entered her own gate and before she could bolt it, defendant forced open the gate and struck her on the right cheek. She telephoned the matter to the French Police and they took her to the Ste. Marie Hospital for treatment; she was later given a medical certificate by the Country Hospital.

In the cross-examination by Mr. Hartopp, the complainant denied that she had worked herself up after learning that Mr. Keet had informed the French Police of her building alterations and that her report of an assault was an imaginary one. She strongly denied that she was an unpleasant neighbour with: "It isn't true, it's the other way around!"

Only one witness was brought up in court yesterday, Mrs. Palmer-Baker bringing forward her Chinese amah to testify. Witness could throw little light on the assault as she heard only the altercation from inside the house and when she had come out saw only her mistress trying to close the gate on the defendant. Witness declared that she saw a black mark on her employer's face—but it was on the left side.

The case was adjourned at this point without the defendant having yet been called to give his evidence.

英籍男子面临殴打指控

昨日，在H.M. 警察法庭（H. M. Police Court）， registrar C. H. Haines 主持审理了一起案件。E. C. Palmer-Baker 女士对 D. G. J. Keet 先生提起殴打指控，称后者用紧握的拳头击打其面部。这起据称发生的袭击事件源于两位邻居之间长期的敌意。据称，袭击发生于6月19日晚，地点在保罗·勒让德路3号（Route Paul Legendre, 3）316弄堂口的原告住所入口处。

Haines 法官将听证会延期至下周一，以便原告传唤证人提供医疗证据。

在昨日的庭审过程中，身为老年妇女的原告表现出明显的痛苦迹象，在被告辩护律师交叉询问的某个阶段，她甚至失声痛哭。Palmer-Baker 女士未由律师代理出庭；因不熟悉法庭程序，她在多个场合需由法官就法律程序事项予以指导。被告由 E. L. Hartopp 律师代理，并 pleaded not guilty（辩称无罪）。

长期摩擦

昨日案件的两位主要当事人是保罗·勒让德路3号316弄的隔壁邻居。法庭披露，双方之间的摩擦由来已久。据悉，Palmer-Baker 女士与 Keet 先生在多个问题上存在争执：双方对弄堂的通行权持有异议；原告反对被告种植的花卉蔓延至其花园；她还反对 Keet 先生在共用围栏上放置数个蜂箱；另一方面，被告则不赞成弄堂大门敞开。原告还主张，Keet 先生曾向法国巡捕房举报其未经许可开始的建筑工程，以此“告发”她。

据称，正是这一系列不满导致了6月19日晚8时30分左右发生的袭击事件。根据 Palmer-Baker 女士的证词，当时她将几位女性友人送至弄堂大门口。在返回自家途中，Keet 先生从屋内冲出并喊道：“你为什么让大门开着？”原告称她并未理会他，因为大门当时已经关闭。

报警处理

随后，当她进入自家院门且尚未及插上门栓时，被告强行推开门并击打其右脸颊。她随即电话通知法国巡捕房，警方将其送往圣玛丽医院（Ste. Marie Hospital）接受治疗；此后，她又从 Country Hospital（乡村医院/公济医院？）获得了一份医疗证明。

在 Hartopp 律师的交叉询问中，原告否认自己在得知 Keet 先生向法国巡捕房举报其建筑改建后情绪激动，也否认其殴打报告是虚构的。她强烈否认自己是个难相处的邻居，并称：“这不是真的，事实恰恰相反！”

昨日法庭仅传唤了一名证人，即 Palmer-Baker 女士带来的中国女佣（amah）。该证人未能就袭击事件提供太多线索，因为她仅在屋内听到争吵声，待她出来时，只看到女主人正试图将被告关在门外。证人宣称她看到雇主脸上有一处黑印——但位于左侧。

案件在此刻休庭，被告尚未被传唤作证。
